topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's themes on cancer transformation and genetics and outlines the learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor Virology and Cellular Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the investigation of transmissible tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for measuring cell transformation.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Genetics of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the functional definitions, cell cycle pathways, and allelic mutation dynamics that distinguish oncogenes from tumor suppressor genes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Cellular Consequences of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how defects in DNA repair, replication proofreading, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-Step Tumor Progression and Hereditary Cancer Predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the stepwise accumulation of somatic and germline mutations in cancer development and how inherited defects accelerate tumorigenesis and influence tumor evolution.

topics.label: Closing Remarks and Reading Recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, offers to answer questions, recommends a book, and previews the next lecture on cancer hallmarks.
